advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Verify the scratch-unavailable refusal detects an unmounted-but-writable mountpoint (e.g. a mount/liveness probe), not just a store_root() OSError, so admission does not write to the root FS after an unmount.
evidence: gate_admission catches only OSError from _slot_dir(): `try:\n directory = _slot_dir()\n except OSError as exc:` then raises GateScratchUnavailableError
_slot_dir -> store_root() -> `root.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)` (repo_snapshot.py:161) succeeds when the mountpoint dir is writable on the root FS
doc claim: docs/plan-review-gate.md 'If the scratch volume itself is unreachable the gate is refused with gate_scratch_unavailable'
advisory.finding: GateScratchUnavailableError only fires when store_root()/mkdir raises OSError. If the dedicated scratch volume is unmounted but its mountpoint directory still exists and is writable on the root filesystem, store_root() succeeds and the gate is ADMITTED, writing snapshot/clone bytes onto the root filesystem — the exact failure ADR 0112's split volume and this refusal exist to prevent. The docs promise 'An unreachable store root refuses', but 'unmounted-but-writable-underneath' is a common unmount outcome that is not detected.
scenarios: scratch volume unmounted; its mountpoint dir remains present and writable on root FS
gate then runs and repopulates snapshot bytes onto the root filesystem undetected

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Decide whether a None admission outcome should still be treated as retryable (fail-safe to backpressure) rather than defaulting to exit 1 / retryable:false.
evidence: _admission_outcome: `except ImportError:  # pragma: no cover ...\n        return None`
GateCongestedError docstring: 'Without it the MCP payload would say retryable: false and the CLI would exit 1: shed load that nobody retries is a dropped request, not backpressure.'
_llm_error_exit_code returns 11 only `if o is not None and getattr(o, 'retryable', False)` (src/rebar/_cli/_llm_commands.py:91)
dropped.finding: When rebar.llm.failure cannot be imported, _admission_outcome returns None, so GateCongestedError.outcome / GateScratchUnavailableError.outcome is None. The refusal then routes as NON-retryable: MCP reports retryable:false and the CLI exits 1 instead of 11 — silently converting shed load into a dropped request that nobody retries, which the module's own docstring identifies as the failure mode to avoid.
scenarios: rebar.llm.failure import fails (broken/partial install) at the moment a congestion refusal is constructed
